newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Motors says not interested in takeover.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Motors says not interested in takeover.

text.p: Samsung Motors Inc, a unit of South Korea's Samsung Group, said on Monday it was not interested in any hostile takeover deals.
"We are already busy enough in proceeding with our existing plans. We cannot afford to seek any merger and acquisitions," said Han Jae-yoon, Samsung Motors spokesman.
Earlier on Monday, Hyundai Motor Co and five other South Korean automakers said they would take joint action against Samsung over a Samsung report that the local auto industry needed restructuring.
The six companies said the Samsung Group must give up its bid to make cars if an industrial restructuring was inevitable.
Samsung has said the report did not represent the company's official position.
"We don't see the need to respond to an episode that flared over a private document," said a Samsung statement.
But analysts said Samsung, despite its denials, probably was interested in a takeover deal as a short-cut to its expansion.
"We cannot possibly think of Samsung succeeding in the car industry without it taking over any existing company," said an analyst at LG Economic Research Institute.

Analysts said Samsung was now troubled to go ahead with its plans to build 500,000 cars by 2002 because of higher-than-expected construction costs and difficulties obtaining technology from its Japanese partner Nissan Motor Co.
